profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap point in Porto San Giorgio, on Italy's Adriatic coast, tagged telecom=data_center, is named Studio BETA SRLS. "SRLS" is the Italian legal designation for a simplified limited-liability company, a structure commonly used by small startups, freelancers, and professional practices due to its lower minimum capital requirements, and "Studio" again indicates a professional-services or design practice in Italian usage. As with the similarly named Studio Delta Srl record elsewhere in this dataset, this pattern points to a small office rather than a data-center business. This entry documents the likely mistag rather than fabricating data-center specifications for what is, by its own name, a small professional-services firm.

reading.body:
A single OpenStreetMap point in Porto San Giorgio, Italy, tagged as a data center, is almost certainly a small professional-services office instead. The name Studio BETA SRLS carries two markers of that: "Studio," which in Italian usage denotes a practice or office, and "SRLS," the simplified limited-liability form used by small firms and freelancers.

The record reports zero megawatts and no operator, no website, and no suitability score. Its only substantive attributes are a name, a coordinate, and an airport 36 miles away in Falconara Marittima. Nothing in the entry describes a building that houses compute.

The pattern matters because datasets of AI infrastructure are assembled from volunteered geographic data, and volunteered tags are only as good as the mapper who applied them. A point like this one, if counted uncritically, inflates the apparent number of facilities without adding a single watt of load. The error runs in the harmless direction here, but the same tagging weakness could just as easily omit a real facility or misplace one.

What this record does not tell the reader is anything about Italian data-center capacity, the Adriatic coast's power or fiber position, or where AI compute in Italy actually sits. It is one point, and the entry itself concludes the tag is wrong.
